paper_metadata.title: Quantum Quantitative Trading: High-Frequency Statistical Arbitrage Algorithm

experiments.description: Variable Time Preselection Algorithm (VTPA) / Quantum Condition Number Comparison Algorithm (QCNCA) for preselecting multicollinear stock portfolios by testing whether a matrix condition number exceeds a threshold.

algorithm.variant: Variable Time Preselection Algorithm with Quantum Condition Number Comparison Algorithm

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Historical stock prices p^(j)_t are loaded via qRAM map |j>|t>|z> -> |j>|t>|z xor p^(j)_t>; portfolios are represented as amplitude-like superpositions over time and stock index registers.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Determine whether a given portfolio matrix has condition number kappa >= kappa_0, used as a proxy for multicollinearity.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Threshold test on condition number; repeated variable-time preselection with clock registers and a stop-flag register.

problem_instance.description: Preselection over portfolios of stocks from a pool of historical quote data; used to identify potentially cointegrated/multicollinear portfolios.

dataset_specification.description: The paper estimates about 8000 stocks in U.S. markets and about N = 1.2 x 10^7 time points from half-second aggregated quotes over 253 trading days; no specific ticker list or date range is given.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical quote data stored in qRAM; no further preprocessing specified for the preselection stage.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical complexity analysis under an assumed uniform distribution of log condition numbers; no empirical runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: qRAM loading of portfolio data; construction of Hermitian block matrix A from design matrix; use of simplified phase estimation subroutines.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement of the flag register and clock registers to decide whether kappa exceeds threshold.

speedup_claims.factor: from O(N^2 d) to O(sqrt(d) kappa_0^2 log(1/epsilon)^2)
speedup_claims.conditions: under the uniform distribution assumption for log condition numbers and qRAM access
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper provides asymptotic analysis only; no empirical benchmark is reported.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N^3) for matrix factorization preselection; benchmark for the overall trading pipeline is stated as O(N^2 d)

experiments.description: Quantum Cointegration Test Algorithm (QCTA) using quantum linear regression followed by a classical Augmented Dickey-Fuller-style stationarity test on residuals.

algorithm.variant: Quantum linear regression-based cointegration test with hybrid classical postprocessing

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Design matrix X and target vector y are amplitude-encoded / accessed through qRAM procedures Px and Py; residuals are computed classically after quantum regression.
problem_formulation.objective_function: First regression estimates beta = X^dagger y; residuals u = y - X beta are then tested for stationarity via an ADF regression on delta u_t = alpha + beta t + gamma u_{t-1} + sum_i delta_i delta u_{t-i} + epsilon_t; cointegration is accepted if the DF statistic passes the critical value test.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hybrid pipeline: quantum regression for coefficients, classical matrix multiplication and subtraction for residuals, then a second regression and classical critical-value comparison.

problem_instance.description: Cointegration verification for a preselected stock portfolio using historical price time series.

dataset_specification.description: Historical stock prices over about 1.2 x 10^7 time points; no explicit ticker set or date range is provided.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Residual construction from first quantum regression; lagged residuals formed by first differences; ADF test compared against Fuller critical values.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical complexity analysis only; no numerical experiments, no train/test split, and no repeated trials reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct residuals via quantum linear regression, then compute predicted values and residuals classically; form lagged residuals for the ADF regression.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute DF statistic gamma_hat / SE(gamma_hat) classically and compare with critical values from Fuller.

results.value: O(d^2.5 kappa^3 / delta^2 poly(log2(d kappa / delta)) + dN + (L+2)^2.5 kappa'^3 / delta'^2 poly(log2((L+2) kappa' / delta')))

classical_baselines.method_name: classical residual generation via matrix multiplication and subtraction

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial improvement in the first regression subroutine via quantum linear regression
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming qRAM access and well-behaved design matrix singular values
speedup_claims.caveats: The overall pipeline remains hybrid and includes classical postprocessing; no empirical speedup is shown.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(d^2.5 kappa^3 / delta^2 poly(log2(d kappa / delta)) + dN + (L+2)^2.5 kappa'^3 / delta'^2 poly(log2((L+2) kappa' / delta')))
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N log N kappa^2 epsilon^-3) for an alternative classical/quantum-inspired residual-generation method; residual multiplication/subtraction costs O(Nd) classically

experiments.description: End-to-end quantum statistical arbitrage pipeline with fixed condition-number preselection followed by quantum cointegration testing.

hyperparameters.d: number of stocks in one portfolio

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio pool P is loaded into quantum registers; each portfolio p is represented by a superposition over time and stock indices, then filtered by VTPA and verified by QCT.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find cointegrated stock portfolios from a pool by first selecting portfolios with condition number above kappa_0 and then testing cointegration.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Two-stage hybrid filtering: quantum preselection by condition number threshold, then quantum regression plus classical ADF test.

problem_instance.description: High-frequency statistical arbitrage on U.S. stock market historical data.

dataset_specification.description: About 8000 stocks and about 1.2 x 10^7 time points from half-second aggregated quotes over 253 trading days.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: qRAM loading of historical quotes; portfolio construction from stock pools; no further preprocessing specified.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical analysis and realistic-case complexity estimate; no empirical benchmark runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: qRAM loading, portfolio enumeration, and classical postprocessing of the ADF statistic.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare DF statistic with critical value table; output cointegrated portfolios and coefficients.

results.value: O(sqrt(d) kappa_0^2 log(1/epsilon)^2) + QCT complexity from exp_2

speedup_claims.factor: from O(N^2 d) to O(sqrt(d) kappa_0^2 log(1/epsilon)^2) for preselection
speedup_claims.conditions: for fixed condition-number threshold and qRAM access
speedup_claims.caveats: The end-to-end pipeline includes the QCT stage, so the quoted speedup is mainly for the preselection stage.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(d) kappa_0^2 log(1/epsilon)^2) for preselection plus QCT complexity from exp_2
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N^3) matrix factorization benchmark; overall classical benchmark stated as O(N^2 d)

experiments.description: End-to-end quantum statistical arbitrage pipeline with progressive preselection over increasing condition-number thresholds until only k portfolios remain, then cointegration testing.

algorithm.variant: Progressive preselection quantum statistical arbitrage pipeline

hyperparameters.d: number of stocks in one portfolio

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio matrices are loaded repeatedly; at each step a larger threshold kappa_j = 2^j is used to discard low-condition-number portfolios until K <= k, then QCT is applied.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Reduce the portfolio pool to a small set of likely multicollinear portfolios and then test cointegration.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Iterative elimination based on condition-number threshold; portfolios failing the threshold are removed from the pool.

problem_instance.description: Same high-frequency stock portfolio search problem, but with unknown condition-number threshold and a target number of remaining portfolios k.

dataset_specification.description: Same U.S. stock market historical quote data as above; no additional dataset split or ticker list is given.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Repeated qRAM loading and iterative portfolio pruning; no further preprocessing specified.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical complexity analysis only; no empirical evaluation reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Iterative threshold schedule and portfolio removal; qRAM loading of each portfolio at each step.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Cointegration testing on the remaining portfolios and classical DF-statistic comparison.

results.value: Repeated use of O(sqrt(d) kappa_j^2 log(1/epsilon)^2) preselection plus QCT

speedup_claims.factor: progressive thresholding reduces the number of tested portfolios
speedup_claims.conditions: when the condition-number threshold is unknown and only k portfolios should remain
speedup_claims.caveats: No closed-form total complexity is given; the paper only states that repeated preselection is used until K <= k.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Progressive thresholding reduces the number of tested portfolios; no single closed-form total complexity beyond repeated use of O(sqrt(d) kappa_j^2 log(1/epsilon)^2) preselection and QCT
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N^3) matrix factorization benchmark; overall classical benchmark stated as O(N^2 d)
